issues.section: §4 last bullet, §11, §1 'Resmî karar verisi yok', §3 windows, §7 atoms
issues.problem: Forfeited (hükmen) results are already in the match data, dated on the original match day. The contract's rule that 'later official decisions never enter predictions or features before the decision date' therefore cannot be enforced as written. I checked the store: 72 of the 102 rows with missing HT are 3-0 or 0-3, and 71 of those have no shot statistics. These are almost certainly forfeits. They cluster in test-period years (22 in 2019, 30 in 2023). §2 only marks these rows İY/MS UNKNOWN. Nothing stops their FT result from entering the next matches' windows (SON3_MAGLUBIYET, SON5_GALIBIYET_EN_AZ_4, SON5_GALIBIYETSIZ, points average, FORM_BEKLENTI, S1 features 5/6/11, rest days). The forfeit was usually decided days or weeks after the date, so the team's next matches are scored using a result that was not known at their decision_time. The main pipeline is inconsistent with this: features.py:246-247 skips non-clean rows entirely, so S0 never sees them while the sequence features would.
issues.fix: Add a rule to §1/§3: any row with missing HT and FT in {3-0, 0-3, 5-0, 0-5}, or with no match statistics and a 3-0/0-3 score, is flagged POSSIBLE_AWARDED. In every pre-match window it is treated as 'result unknown', the same as a missing match (counts use n_known, and the window is flagged incomplete). It is never a G/B/M outcome and never a label. It still counts for rest days and match order, because the fixture existed. Report how many rows were flagged per period. As a sensitivity run, also flag rows that are 3-0/0-3 with HT 0-0 and no statistics (610 rows).

issues.section: §1 alias bullet ('Ana modeller etkilenmez'), §6 S0/S1/S2, §7 FAVORI / FORM_BEKLENTI
issues.problem: The sequence module merges renamed teams through sequences/aliases.py, but S0 does not. S0's strengths come from features.py, which keeps per-league state keyed by the raw team string (features.py:227-247). A new name is treated as a new or promoted team: DC promoted_attack/defense is -0.1, Elo uses its promoted rating, and DC parameters are estimated only from matches played under the new name. Nott'm Forest (from 2024-12-26, mid-season E0) and M'gladbach (from 2025-01-11) therefore get a cold-start S0 for the rest of 2024/25, which is in the test period, while their sequence features still carry their full history. Any form or sequence feature then shows 'added value over S0' for these teams, and that comes purely from S0 losing their identity. The same problem affects FAVORI, E = Σp0, the null draws and S2's S0 strength inputs. It also produces UNEXPLAINED_ANOMALY records for the same teams. Separately, the alias table is built by looking over the whole date range. Real-world club identity is legitimately known at the time, but the contract does not say the table must be built blind to outcomes or frozen.
issues.fix: Choose one option and write it into the contract: (a) rebuild the S0 inputs used by the research module (features plus per-season M10 refits) on canonicalised team IDs from aliases.py, leaving the production models untouched; or (b) exclude from all evaluation, and from the null, every team-row whose team, or whose opponent, had an alias break in the previous 60 league matches or the previous 400 days, and report the count. Also state that the alias table is built only from names, leagues and date ranges (never from outcomes), is frozen before the first pattern result, and has its SHA-256 in the manifest.

issues.section: §6 S0 (2-parameter recalibration), §6 S1 feature 6, §7 FORM_BEKLENTI_*, §6 S2 E, §5 Isınma
issues.problem: The contract never says which S0 prediction is used for a past match. Feature 6, FORM_BEKLENTI_USTU/ALTI and S2's E use 'S0 expected' values for the last 10 matches or for neighbour rows. The recalibration is fit on 'S0 predictions of previous seasons'. If the implementation applies the current fold's S0 to past matches, those matches are inside that model's training set, so the values are in-sample: residuals shrink and the recalibration learns in-sample optimism. The warm-up claim also does not match the code. validation.py sets BURN_IN_LAST=2002, so walk_forward only trains on fold ≥2003. That gives no out-of-sample S0 for 2003/04 (the null already falls back to base rates there). The 2004/05 recalibration then has no earlier out-of-sample season, and FORM_BEKLENTI/feature 6 have no valid S0 expectation for 2003/04 matches in the first 2004/05 windows.
issues.fix: Add an 'S0 lineage' rule. Every match has exactly one stored S0 prediction, made by the fold whose training data ends before that match's season (training max date < the match's decision_time), keyed by event_id with fold_id and model hash. Every downstream use (expected points, recalibration training, S2 E, FAVORI, the null) reads that table and nothing else. Recalibration for season Y is fit only on stored predictions from seasons in [first out-of-sample season, Y-1], and is the identity until at least one full out-of-sample season exists. Window matches without a stored S0 count as missing for features 6/FORM_BEKLENTI, and the atom is NaN (excluded) until 10 matches with S0 exist. Either explicitly relax BURN_IN_LAST to 2001 for the research S0 or move the warm-up/keşif boundary, and state which.

issues.problem: The null draws only one of the 9 İY/MS classes per match, yet §7 requires every outcome-based atom to be recomputed from the draws. SON10_2Y_GOL_FARKI_EN_AZ_5 (second-half goal difference over the last 10) cannot be computed from an HT/FT sign alone. An implementation will either quietly use real goals, which puts real outcomes into the null, or drop or approximate the atom. In either case the null no longer re-runs the same 840-hypothesis search, and the dependence structure behind Westfall-Young max|z| is distorted.
issues.fix: Draw the full score in the null: (H1 home, H1 away, H2 home, H2 away) from the same tilted, q-calibrated S0 joint grid (joint_probs/joint_regions already contain the H1×H2 structure). The tail beyond the grid gets a stated rule, e.g. a draw from the marginal tail cells. Derive İY/MS, G/B/M, points and second-half goal difference from the drawn score. Add a unit test asserting that no column of the real results table is read inside the null loop: run the null with real fthg/ftag/hthg/htag set to NaN and require identical output.

issues.section: §6 S0 recalibration vs §7 E = Σp0 and the null
issues.problem: The null outcomes come from S0's raw 9-cell distribution. O−E and z, however, use p0, which (per §6) is the per-target 2-parameter recalibrated probability fit on real outcomes. In the null replicates E is then not the expectation of the generating process, so every null z has a built-in bias that the real-data z does not have (or the reverse). The max|z| reference distribution and the FWER/BY p-values become miscalibrated in an unknown direction. Recalibrating four targets separately also cannot be expressed as one coherent 9-cell distribution to sample from.
issues.fix: Make the reference distribution and E the same object. Either (a) recalibrate at the 9-cell level (for example multinomial bias/temperature on the 9 log-probabilities, fit on stored out-of-sample predictions of earlier seasons), and use those cells both for the draws and for every target's p0; or (b) run the search and the null on raw S0 cells and use the 2-parameter recalibration only as the offset in S1/S2/hazard. Write the choice into config, and in the null check that the mean z per hypothesis is ≈0 (|mean| < 0.1 over R).

issues.problem: (1) Purging happens only 'at period boundaries'. The recalibration is refit every season, and the refit schedule for S1, S2 and the hazard model in the parametre and test periods is not stated (frozen after keşif? refit each season?). Any refit cutoff inside a period that uses post-event targets ('sonraki 3 maç'; labels up to 400 days ahead, across the summer break) needs the same purge. (2) label_known_at = 'match day' is compared against a boundary that falls on the same day as test decision_times (00:00), so whether ties are purged is undefined. (3) Post-event labels are 'unknown → not evaluated' when the team leaves the covered tiers (relegation out of the lowest covered league). Survival in coverage, a future fact correlated with poor end-of-season form, then selects which rows are evaluated.
issues.fix: Replace the bullet with a general rule. For every fit with cutoff T (the first decision_time of the block being predicted), training rows must have label_known_at < T, where label_known_at = (day of the k-th later match) + 1 day 00:00, so the match must be finished. Specify the S1/S2/hazard protocol explicitly: e.g. fit on keşif, select C/k on parametre, refit on keşif+parametre with purge, then freeze for test with no refit inside test, or else refit per season with purge. For 'next k matches' targets, model departures from coverage as censoring. Report the share of rows censored by coverage exit per period, and run a sensitivity analysis restricting to teams that stay in coverage the following season, so the selection effect is visible and not hidden.

issues.problem: SEZON_SONU = order ≥ 0.8×2×(n_teams−1) has three time and definition faults. (a) n_teams and the season length are not knowable from the data before the season unless they come from a frozen table. A distinct-team count over the whole league-season uses rows not yet played, and undercounts in partial seasons (2026/27 in the data, coverage gaps). (b) The formula is wrong for 6 of the 22 leagues with split or play-off formats (SC0–SC3, B1, G1). For example, SC2/SC3 have 10 teams and 36 matches, so the atom fires from match 15 of 36. (c) §5 assigns seasons by date with a July cut, but 554 matches of 2019/20 in 9 leagues (E0, E1, G1, I1, I2, P1, SP1, SP2, T1) were played in Jul/Aug 2020 (verified). With a date-based season key, the real end-of-season matches of 2019/20 become 2020/21 matches 1–9, and every 2020/21 ordinal in those leagues is shifted by about 9, so SEZON_SONU fires early throughout a test season.
issues.fix: Use two keys: the in-season ordinal and SEZON_SONU use the data's 'season' column, and fold/period/refit boundaries use date. State this, and assert that each S0 fold's training max date < the predicted rows' min date. Define the season length from a frozen config table of scheduled league matches per team for each league-season, built from regulations before any result. If such a table is not feasible, use the maximum per-team match count of the same league in the previous season (known before the season starts). Drop G1/B1/SC* from SEZON_SONU if neither is reliable, and record that in the contract before keşif runs.

issues.problem: The A/B/C check gives no periods and no M10 offset source. The only M10 out-of-sample predictions are dev 2008–2018 (goal_dev_tur7_pred.pkl) and test 2019–2026. experiments.jsonl record 7 used 2019–2026 once as the final A/B/C test, and record 9 says any variant needs a new holdout. Evaluating 'M10 + sequence features' on 2018/19–2025/26 (§5 Test) would look at an already-spent A/B/C holdout a second time. Using the production M10 artifact (trained on all data) as the offset would put in-sample predictions into the offset.
issues.fix: State that the A/B/C offset is the stored walk-forward M10 prediction for each match (from its own fold; never the production artifact). The check fits on 2008–2012 and evaluates on 2013–2018 inside dev, with C chosen by inner time-split on 2008–2012. Any 2019+ A/B/C number is labelled EXPLORATORY (holdout spent, record 7/9) and cannot give OUT_OF_SAMPLE_SUPPORTED. Confirmation is prospective only, on matches after the contract date.

issues.problem: Prospective status depends on 'forward paper tracking on post-contract matches', but nothing requires the forecast to exist before the match. Data arrives in batches after matches are played. A 'prospective' run computed after a DataStore update is really a backtest on matches after the contract date, and could even run after a definition change. The contract also reads 'resmî karar' only as federation rulings. It never defines the system's own dated decision records, which is what gates official decisions in this codebase (the append-only, hash-chained ledger in goals/ledger.py; decide() blocks at or after kickoff).
issues.fix: Add: a forecast or pattern trigger counts toward PAPER_TRADING only if it was written to the append-only ledger (or a dedicated research ledger with the same hash chain) with a timezone-aware created_at < decision_time (match day 00:00 local). It must also carry the contract version, the config hash, and the S0 model hash trained only on data before that date. Rows created later are excluded and counted. Fixtures come from the existing fixture source in engine.py, never from the results store.

issues.problem: The honesty note understates how much S0's design has already seen. M10's variant choice and hyperparameters (xi=0.0019, ridge, promoted priors, REFIT_DAYS, shrink, C1_FEATURES) were selected on DEV_YEARS 2008–2018 (validation.py:25). That range overlaps keşif and parametre and includes 2018/19, the first season of §5 Test. The inspection also ran an in-sample HT/FT calibration of the joint model on 52,902 rows from 2019-07 onward, which goes beyond 'aggregate HT/FT frequencies'. S0 is therefore a design tuned on those periods, which biases O−E toward 0 there and makes the 2018/19 test season partly design-seen.
issues.fix: Expand the note: S0 hyperparameters were tuned on 2008–2018 (including 2018/19), and the S0 HT/FT path was calibration-checked in-sample on 2019+. Freeze every S0 setting and hash it in the manifest now. Either start Test at 2019/20 or label 2018/19 'S0 design-seen'. Add a sensitivity run with an untuned baseline (e.g. M0_taban-derived HT/FT cells).

sound_parts: decision_time = match day 00:00 with every same-day match excluded (including other games in the league). This matches the day-batched update in features.py:234-249, which computes all features for a day before adding any of that day's results.

Mirror rows: both team rows share event_id/pair_id and stay together in splits, bootstrap and the null. Periods are cut by date, so a match's two rows can never land in different periods, and ISO-week blocks keep them together.

S2 exclusions (the query match, its mirror row, every same-day row, and only rows whose labels are known before decision_time) are correct for leakage. Fitting the scaler on pre-match features from keşif only leaks no outcomes.

Post-event windows not yet played are left censored and never filled with zeros, and label_known_at is defined as the day of the k-th later match, not as a match count. This handles summer-break horizons.

The null keeps S0 strengths fixed from real outcomes and the contract says so openly. Under H0 (outcomes follow S0 given the past) the martingale property still holds, so this alone does not invalidate the max|z| reference.
2026/27 matches already in the dataset (Aug–Sep 2026) are excluded from prospective tracking, and S0p (Bet365 odds of unknown timing) stays secondary and never gates a status.

issues.problem: The null and the observed statistic do not use the same baseline. The null draws one HT/FT outcome from 'S0'ın 9 İY/MS olasılıkları', which is the un-recalibrated tilted distribution. E = Σp0, however, uses the S0 team-target probability, and §6 recalibrates each team target with its own 2-parameter logistic. The inspection measured reversal cells about 7-12% below observed (around 4 SE on 52,902 rows), so recalibration moves p0 for GERIDEN_GALIBIYET/ONDEN_MAGLUBIYET by a similar amount. In every replicate the reversal-target z values would then be biased by roughly -5 on the discovery pool (about 128k team rows, E≈2.9k, a 10% gap). Because the null takes max|z| over all 840 hypotheses, its critical value inflates and the FWER calibration is meaningless for all four targets. A second problem: four independent binary recalibrations cannot be consistent with each other. The home row's GALIBIYET and the away row's MAGLUBIYET are the same event but would get different p0, so mirror-equivalent hypotheses get different E.
issues.fix: Replace the four per-target 2-parameter recalibrations with ONE 9-class recalibration of the S0 HT/FT distribution: a multinomial logit with the S0 log-probabilities as offset, 9 cell intercepts plus one temperature, fitted on prior seasons only. Derive every team target (both perspectives) from the recalibrated 9 cells. Use exactly that distribution for both E (real data) and the draws (null), and keep the recalibration fixed across replicates. Add a unit test: across null replicates, the mean of O−E for each of the 840 hypotheses is within MC error of 0.

issues.problem: The search space contains context atoms that are not sequence atoms: EV_SAHIBI, FAVORI, KISA_DINLENME and SEZON_SONU. Alone or paired, these test whether S0 is calibrated within a subgroup, not whether sequences carry information. With discovery-sized pools, small stratum miscalibration gives huge z values. Example: GALIBIYET × EV_SAHIBI has about 64k rows and E≈29k, so a 2% home-advantage drift gives z≈4.6, enough to pass WY. A favourite–longshot bias does the same for FAVORI. The parametric null is perfectly calibrated by construction, so it cannot absorb this. Ranking by |z| then hands the top-5 slots to the largest-n context conditions. Such miscalibration persists, so it can survive the parameter and test periods and the log-loss criterion and receive OUT_OF_SAMPLE_SUPPORTED. The result would be reported as a 'pattern' even though it is a calibration artefact, which contradicts the user's aim of measuring added information from sequences.
issues.fix: (1) Remove the four context atoms from the pattern space as stand-alone conditions. Use them only as stratifiers, with HAS_HISTORY_ATOM required in every tested condition. (2) Compute the expectation by indirect standardisation within strata s = target × home/away × league × season × S0-probability quintile (× FAVORI / KISA_DINLENME / SEZON_SONU): E_adj = Σ_i p0_i · (O_s / E_s), with O_s and E_s taken over all rows of the stratum. This is a Mantel–Haenszel-type contrast of condition against complement within the stratum, so stratum-level miscalibration cancels. Apply the identical statistic in every null replicate. (3) Report the context-atom O/E values in a separate 'S0 calibration diagnostics' table that never receives pattern statuses.

issues.problem: The variance Σp0(1−p0) is right only under a sharp martingale null with one row per match; overlapping windows are not the issue there. It fails in two ways that point in opposite directions. (a) Mirror rows: when both rows of a match qualify (common for SON5_GALIBIYETSIZ, SON3_MAGLUBIYET, or own∧rakip pairs), the outcomes are mutually exclusive. For GALIBIYET with p_h=.45, p_a=.30, d=.25 the true variance is d(1−d)=.19 against a naive .46, so z is deflated by about 1.5×. This distorts the |z| ranking and lowers the power of single-step max-|z|, because hypotheses no longer share a common scale. (b) Under the weaker null that matters here (no sequence effect, but S0 has persistent team-season errors), residuals Y−p0 are positively correlated within team-season. Σp(1−p) then understates Var(O−E), and the parametric null (independent draws given p0) has no such dependence, so the procedure is anti-conservative. The Poisson O/E interval is a third, inconsistent variance: for p≈0.4 it overstates the binomial variance by 1/(1−p)≈1.6×, so the 'interval excludes 1' gate contradicts the z gate.
issues.fix: Compute Var(O−E) at match level from the (recalibrated) 9-cell distribution: for each match, the exact variance of the sum of its qualifying rows' indicators, including the −p_h·p_a covariance. To cover the team-season dependence, estimate a team-season log-odds random-effect variance σ²_target by method of moments on warm-up and discovery residual totals, and add that random effect to the null draws. Report the σ=0 run as a sensitivity check. Alternatively, use a league-season cluster-robust (CR2) variance in both the real data and every replicate. Teams never play in two leagues in one season (verified), so league-season clusters nest the pair, the team-season and the week. Replace the Poisson interval with O/E ± 1.96·√Var/E from the same variance, or with the cluster-bootstrap interval.

issues.section: §7 Referans süreç ve çoklu test (R=200, WY, BY)
issues.problem: R=200 is too few for FWER decisions at 0.05. The adjusted p has resolution 1/201, and its Monte Carlo SE near 0.05 is √(.05·.95/200)≈0.015, so p_adj=0.05 means somewhere in 0.02–0.08 and borderline admissions depend on the seed. BY is unspecified and degenerate as written. If its p-values come from the same 200 replicates, the minimum is 1/201≈0.005, while BY's first threshold with m=840 is 0.05/(840·H_840)≈8e-6, so BY can never reject. The selection rule says 'Düzeltilmiş p < 0,05' without saying whether that is WY or BY. The contract also does not say that the support filter (n≥500, E≥25) is reapplied inside each replicate. Support of history-atom conditions depends on the simulated outcomes, so the replicate maximum must be taken over the hypotheses that are supported in that replicate.
issues.fix: Set R≥1000 (MC SE≈0.007), or use sequential Besag–Clifford stopping with a pre-stated rule. Report the MC 99% interval of every p_adj, and label hypotheses whose interval straddles 0.05 INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. The cost is small because only atoms and sums are recomputed, never features or S0. Use Westfall–Young step-down maxT, which has the same FWER and more power, as the sole selection criterion. Compute BY from two-sided normal p-values of the corrected z and use it for reporting only. In each replicate, apply the support filter and then take the max over the supported set.

issues.problem: Taking the top 5 by |z| from 210 conditions that include all 190 pairs fills the slots with nested and duplicate versions of one effect. If atom A is strong, A∧B for many B also have large |z|, and slots go to 'A∧EV_SAHIBI', 'A∧FAVORI' and so on. Each would later be reported as a two-atom pattern when only A matters. The four targets also form two mirror pairs (GALIBIYET↔MAGLUBIYET, GERIDEN_GALIBIYET↔ONDEN_MAGLUBIYET), and RAKIP_SON3_MAGLUBIYET and RAKIP_SON5_IY_ONDE_EN_AZ_3 mirror their own-team atoms. So (RAKIP_SON3_MAGLUBIYET, GALIBIYET) is the same set of matches and events as (SON3_MAGLUBIYET, MAGLUBIYET). The '840 hypotheses' count therefore includes exact duplicates that can take two of the five slots.
issues.fix: Before counting and selection, canonicalise each (condition, target) as a set of event-level (match, cell) pairs and drop exact mirror duplicates. Log both the unique count and the 840. Admit a pair A∧B only if it beats both of its single atoms, using a z with E recomputed from a baseline that already includes the better single atom (an interaction test inside the same WY framework). Select the top 5 by the lower confidence bound of |log O/E|, with at most one candidate per maximal atom family.

issues.problem: Four gaps in the out-of-sample criteria. (1) No multiplicity control at the test stage: up to 5 candidates reach test, each judged at 95%, so family-wise error can reach about 23%. (2) The contract does not say where the 'S0 + örüntü göstergesi' coefficient is estimated. If it is fitted on test rows, the log-loss gain is in-sample. (3) ISO-week block bootstrap treats weeks as independent. Log-loss differences carry S0's team-season errors, which persist across weeks, so the intervals are too narrow; the same flaw affects every §9 interval. (4) 'Aynı yönde' and the Holm test do not state whether they are one- or two-sided, and the status rule does not say whether the O/E interval is required in each period or pooled.
issues.fix: Fix the indicator's log-odds coefficient from discovery plus parameter data, with the S0 offset, and apply it unchanged to test. Bootstrap test Δlog-loss and O/E with league-season clusters (≈22×8 = 176 clusters in test; they nest pairs, team-seasons and weeks). Keep ISO-week blocks only as a sensitivity check. Require the one-sided upper bound at level 1−0.05/k < 0, where k is the number of candidates reaching test (Holm). State that the parameter-period Holm test and the test-period O/E criterion are one-sided in the pre-registered direction and are evaluated separately in each period.

issues.problem: The duration categories are confounded with unobserved team heterogeneity. Teams with a higher latent comeback rate, such as strong second-half sides, have short gaps. Even if each team's hazard were constant, the pooled hazard would fall with 'matches since last event' (dynamic selection, the frailty artefact), and the discovery LRT would report duration dependence that does not exist. The S0 offset does not remove this: S0 under-predicts reversals by 7-12%, and that shortfall differs by team. The LRT also assumes independent rows, but rows of the same team share the frailty, so its p-value is anti-conservative. Finally, 'henüz gözlenmedi' pools data-start truncation, entry from uncovered tiers and alias breaks. These have different composition across periods, so the category is not comparable between discovery and test.
issues.fix: Add a team-level frailty: either a team-season random intercept (GLMM with the S0 offset), or a pre-spell covariate equal to the team's shrunken own event rate over the previous two seasons. Test the duration categories conditional on it. Replace the LRT with a cluster-robust Wald test (clusters = team), or calibrate it by parametric bootstrap from S0 plus the estimated frailty with no duration effect; that bootstrap should reject about 5% of the time. Split 'henüz gözlenmedi' into 'veri başlangıcı' and 'kapsama giriş/kopukluk', or start the at-risk time at each team's first observed event (standard left-truncation handling) and report the excluded rows.

issues.problem: As written, the control is either meaningless or circular. If the random target is generated independently of S0 (for example, a constant p), E=Σp0 is the wrong expectation and z is uninterpretable. If it is generated from S0, it is just one more null replicate, and WY controls its FWER by construction. Either way it cannot detect the real threats: S0 miscalibration, team-season dependence and mirror structure in the real outcomes. It is the contract's only empirical check of null calibration.
issues.fix: Use a negative-control placebo built on REAL outcomes and the real S0. For each team-row, replace the history atoms with those of a different team from the same league-season, matched on S0 strength decile and schedule position, so the atoms carry no information about this team's outcome. Then run the full pipeline: search, WY, selection. Repeat for at least 20 seeds and pre-register the pass rule: at most 1 seed in 20 may produce a WY discovery. More than that means the null is anti-conservative and real discoveries are frozen until it is fixed. Keep the synthetic-from-S0 run only as a code test, checking that the rejection rate is about 5%.

issues.problem: The grid C ∈ {0.01, 0.1, 1} is effectively unregularised. With about 128k discovery rows and sklearn's C·Σloss + ½‖w‖² objective, C=0.01 gives a per-observation penalty of about 1/(C·n)≈8e-4 on standardised features, so the three fits are almost identical and the 'selection' just chases noise. The contract also does not say whether features are standardised or whether the intercept, which absorbs global miscalibration, is penalised. sklearn LogisticRegression also does not accept an offset.
issues.fix: Standardise the 12 features using discovery-period statistics. Leave the intercept unpenalised. Parameterise the penalty per observation, λ ∈ {1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1} on the mean log-loss, and include λ=∞ (offset plus intercept only) as the reference. Implement with an offset-capable solver, such as statsmodels GLM fit_regularized or a custom L-BFGS.

issues.problem: The fixed pseudo-count of 20 events implies very different shrinkage across targets. For GERIDEN_GALIBIYET (p≈0.023) at k=200, E≈4.6, so even O=2E moves the odds by only about 19%. For GALIBIYET at k=1000, E≈370 and there is almost no shrinkage. Adding the log of a rate ratio to the logit also under-adjusts common targets: with p0=0.5 and O/E=1.2 the formula gives 0.545, not 0.6. Neighbours drawn from overlapping windows of the same team-run are near-duplicates, so 'distinct matches' overstates the effective sample size.
issues.fix: Express shrinkage in expected-event units with κ chosen jointly with k in the parameter period (κ ∈ {5, 20, 80}), or use empirical-Bayes Gamma shrinkage of O/E fitted in discovery. For targets with p0 > 0.1, apply the ratio on the probability scale, capped, or estimate a log odds-ratio. Report the effective sample size as the number of distinct team-seasons, or as a design-effect-adjusted n.

sound_parts: The core z-statistic is valid under a sharp null despite overlapping windows and repeated teams: if E[Y_i | past] = p0_i and p0 does not depend on the outcome being tested, O−E is a martingale sum and Σp0(1−p0) is the right variance (for one row per match). The problems listed are mirror rows and the weaker null with team-season errors, not overlap itself.

Re-running the whole search (840 hypotheses) in every null replicate, with outcome-based atoms recomputed from the drawn outcomes, correctly accounts for the selection step. Holding strengths and non-outcome atoms fixed is acceptable for the martingale argument.
Drawing one HT/FT outcome per match keeps the two team rows consistent, and carrying mirror rows together in splits and resampling is correct.

The hypothesis budget is fixed in advance (20 atoms, conditions of length ≤2, 4 targets, no extra search), the discovery, parameter and test periods are separate in time with Holm on ≤5 candidates in an independent period, and the contract openly says the test period is 'closed for conditional patterns, descriptive statistics seen'.

Purging with label_known_at, excluding same-day rows (including the S2 query's mirror row and all same-day rows), and keeping 'next k matches' targets unknown until the k-th match is played prevent leakage of future information into features and labels.

Keeping 'next match' and 'at least once in the next 3' probabilities separate, refusing 'it is overdue' rules, and keeping anomaly scores out of decisions and statuses are statistically sound choices.

lens: Coverage of the user's specification: which required elements the contract leaves out, gets wrong, or specifies too loosely to implement

issues.problem: The user's falsification checklist is only partly in the contract. Covered: the structure-preserving reference process, dependent multiple-testing control, keeping all experiments, and the S0 offset. Not covered at all: (a) removing influential matches, teams or leagues; (b) showing counter-examples, i.e. condition met but no event; (c) comparing against teams of similar strength or a matched control; (d) league and opponent heterogeneity; (e) a stated criterion for cross-year stability, where §9 only says 'sezonlar arası kararlılık' is reported, with no rule. None of these checks feeds into OUT_OF_SAMPLE_SUPPORTED either, so a pattern can pass that status even if one club, one league or two seasons carry it entirely. The S0p check ('piyasa zaten biliyor') is also not a gate. FORM_BEKLENTI_USTU/ALTI are close to detectors of S0 strength lag, so without that gate base-model information gets re-reported as a sequence pattern. This is a pre-registration, so anything left out now cannot be added later as a clean test.
issues.fix: Add a §7b 'Yanlışlama listesi' that is pre-registered and applies to every candidate in both the parameter and test periods. (1) Leave-one-team-out and leave-one-league-out O/E: fail if any single team or league moves O/E across 1 or flips the sign. (2) Drop the top 1% of rows by contribution to O−E, then recompute; it must stay the same direction with its CI excluding 1. (3) Per-season O/E table: at least 60% of seasons in the same direction. (4) Matched comparison: rows without the condition in the same league-season, with the same venue and the same S0-probability decile; report the empirical rate difference. (5) Re-estimate with S0p as the offset: if the effect vanishes, the status is NO_ADDED_VALUE, reason 'piyasa/temel model bilgisi'. (6) List the 20 largest counter-examples in the card. OUT_OF_SAMPLE_SUPPORTED requires checks 1–5 to pass, and the result of each check is stored in experiments.jsonl.

issues.section: §7 (whole), missing Mode A / Mode B definition
issues.problem: Mode A (event-first historical) and Mode B (condition-first validation) are never defined. The statistics in §7 are a condition-first O-vs-E against S0. They omit what the user explicitly asked Mode B to report: the full 2×2 (hits = condition and event; misses = condition and no event; hits without the condition = event and no condition), the base rate in comparable matches, i.e. an empirical comparator and not only the model-based E, and repetition in later years. Uncertainty is a Poisson CI on O/E. That treats team-rows as independent, but overlapping 5- and 10-match windows make the same team satisfy an atom for many consecutive rows, so the CI is too narrow. Mode A selects on the outcome: it looks at the windows before known events. If its output is not explicitly confined to description, it is a channel for informally generating hypotheses on the full period, including the test years.
issues.fix: Add a §7a. Mode A: descriptive only. It runs on any period, never produces a status, and never adds an atom; its output carries the label 'olay seçimli, tahmin değil'. Mode B card fields: n_cond, hits, misses, events_without_cond, the event rate with and without the condition, the matched empirical base rate (league-season × venue × S0 decile), E from S0, absolute difference, relative lift, a CI from an ISO-week block bootstrap clustered on team-season and keeping pair_id together (replacing the Poisson CI), and an O/E table per season for every later year. Mode B is the only source of statuses.

issues.section: §3, §4, §8 (post-event horizon vs pre-match prediction; the Query 1 / Query 2 split)
issues.problem: The contract never separates the user's two questions: what happens in the next 1/3/5 matches after an event (post-event / Query 1), and whether this match's outcome can be predicted from the pre-match sequence (Query 2). Post-event windows are defined (§3) and get a label_known_at (§4), and §8 says 'next' and 'next 3' are kept apart. But no post-event target, statistic, multiplicity control or status is pre-registered: §7 targets are same-match only, and SON_MAC_* atoms cover only k=1. Any post-event result produced later would therefore be unplanned. The overlapping horizons (k=3 or 5 for consecutive events of the same team) are also not addressed in the inference.
issues.fix: Add a section with two parts. Query 1: pre-register a small, fixed set of targets, e.g. for each of the 4 event types, P(win in the next match), P(≥1 same event in the next 3) and points per match over the next 5, each against S0-expected values over the same matches. Evaluate on non-overlapping event instances only, taking the first event per team per k-window, and add these targets to the hypothesis count and to the WY/BY family, or run a separate family with its own null. Query 2 is the existing §7. The UI and reports label every result Q1 or Q2.

issues.problem: The event card the user requires is not specified. There is no PRE_EVENT / EVENT_OUTCOME / POST_EVENT structure. Required fields are missing: match ids, home/away, HT/FT scores, the team-perspective result per match, prev/next match ids, the covered fields per match (HT missing, odds missing, stats missing), source, and timestamps. The 'league only' vs 'all official matches' views are not specified as two views. 'Eksik' is one undifferentiated flag that merges three different situations: (i) the team left the covered tiers (relegation out of the data, or alias breaks such as Sparta → Sparta Rotterdam, 2010–2016), (ii) the 400-day cap, and (iii) right-censoring at the data end. Kickoff timestamps for the mirror source rest on an unverified UK-time assumption, which the critic flagged.
issues.fix: Add an EventCard schema in the contract and in config.py. Header fields: event_id, pair_id, team, opponent, venue, league, season, date, HT/FT, the HTFT_x_y key, team result. Three blocks: PRE_EVENT (5/10), EVENT_OUTCOME and POST_EVENT (1/3/5). Each row carries match_id, prev_id/next_id, venue, half scores, the as-of S0 strengths of both teams, field coverage flags, source, ingestion time, and kickoff time with a 'saat dilimi doğrulanmadı' flag. Window status takes one of {COMPLETE, COVERAGE_EXIT, GAP_GT_400D, RIGHT_CENSORED, HT_MISSING}. The 'tüm resmî maçlar' view tab is always rendered and shows DATA_QUALITY_BLOCKED. The opponent's PRE_EVENT block follows the same schema.

issues.problem: The representation leaves out most of what the user listed. (a) The venue of each past match is missing, so 'HT behind 2 of last 5' is confounded with how many of those were away games. (b) The as-of opponent and own strength for each past match is missing; only the current match's strengths go into S2. (c) Goals per half per match are reduced to one second-half goal-difference sum. (d) Market expectation of past matches is absent, even though 1X2 odds and O/U 2.5 odds (85% of rows) are available. (e) Fixture density uses rest days only, and those are measured from league matches only, so midweek cup and European games are invisible: KISA_DINLENME and feature 12 mismeasure congestion yet are named as if they measure it. (f) The data contains shots, shots on target and red cards (h_sot 66% overall and 93% since 2018; h_red 69% overall and 100% since 2018). The contract neither uses nor excludes them, and it never declares xG or lineups DATA_QUALITY_BLOCKED. (g) S2 'similar sequences' is Euclidean distance on 12 aggregates, not on sequences. Its 'effective sample = distinct matches' ignores that consecutive rows of the same team share 4/5 or 9/10 of their windows, so neighbours are near-duplicates.
issues.fix: Add to S1/S2 and to the event card: per-match venue, the as-of S0 opponent strength, first- and second-half goals for and against, and market surprise (result minus de-vigged 1X2 expectation) where odds exist. Rename the rest variables to LIG_ARASI_GUN and state that cup congestion is DATA_QUALITY_BLOCKED. Explicitly mark xG and lineups DATA_QUALITY_BLOCKED. Decide now, before any result, whether SOT and red cards are allowed as past-match descriptors, and freeze that choice. In S2, cap neighbours at 1 per team-season (or thin each team's windows to non-overlapping ones), and report the numbers of distinct teams and distinct team-seasons alongside distinct matches.

issues.problem: The season-stage atom uses the fixed rule ≥ 0.8 × 2 × (n_teams − 1). In the data, SC0 teams play 33–38 matches against a 22-match double round robin (ratio 1.73), and SC1–SC3 play 36 against 18 (ratio 2.0). The atom therefore fires from match 18 of 38 (about 47% of the season) in SC0, and from match 15 of 36 (about 40%) in SC1–SC3. B1 and G1 reach 1.3×. The 2019/20 seasons cut short by COVID never fire. Because the atom is pre-registered, the error would be frozen into 210 conditions × 4 targets.
issues.fix: Define the stage as team_match_no / expected_matches. expected_matches comes from that league's previous complete season (median matches per team), with an explicit override table for split leagues (SC0–SC3, B1, G1). Seasons where the league-season ended early are marked UNKNOWN. Add a unit test for SC0 and SC1.

issues.problem: S1 needs 5 or 10 prior matches, and S2 needs labelled neighbours. Missing histories are common: season-opening promoted teams, teams entering the data, the 102 HT-missing matches inside windows, and alias breaks. The contract does not say whether these rows are imputed, flagged or dropped, or that S0, S0p, S1 and S2 are scored on identical rows. If S1 drops rows S0 keeps (or the reverse), the log-loss/Brier 'ek katkı' compares different populations. The user requires an M0/M1/M2 comparison on the same matches.
issues.fix: State the rule. Rows with incomplete windows stay in, with features computed over the available matches, a count feature n_available, and a missing indicator; HT-missing matches inside a window are skipped and counted. All of S0, S0p, S1 and S2 are evaluated on one shared row set, the intersection, whose row-id SHA-256 goes into the manifest. Separately, report the size of the excluded set and the S0 metrics on it.

issues.problem: (a) The user asked for a same-match comparison of the sequence-free model, the sequence model and the market reference. §10 does not say S0, S1/S2 and the de-vigged Bet365 1X2 are evaluated on the same matches with the same decision rule, threshold, commission and staking. (b) GALIBIYET for the home row and MAGLUBIYET for the away row are the same 1X2 selection. Counted per team-row, every bet appears twice, which inflates n and narrows the CIs. (c) 'Mevcut EV motoru (goals/value.py)' does not support 1X2. The goals registry holds only goal markets; decide() returns MARKET_UNSUPPORTED for any non-primary market (decision.py:106-109); settle() has no 1X2 result market. Shared settlement/EV is therefore infeasible as written. (d) ROI_UNAVAILABLE does not exist as a token anywhere in the code (the critic verified this).
issues.fix: Specify a single research-only settlement and EV function for FT_1/FT_X/FT_2. It reuses expected_value(p, odds, commission) from value.py; it does not go through decide() and does not change the main registry. Allow one bet per event_id per selection. Evaluate all three probability sources on the same event set with identical threshold, commission and flat stake, using ISO-week block-bootstrap CIs. Define the ROI_UNAVAILABLE constant in sequences/config.py and list the cards and reports where it appears for the HTFT and comeback targets.

issues.problem: (a) The user requires two labels, PREDICTIVE_PATTERN and UNEXPLAINED_ANOMALY. Only the second is defined, and there is no rule for assigning a finding to one or the other. (b) 'Büyük fark' and the surprise threshold are not pre-registered. (c) The checklist calls in-match information 'veri yok → değerlendirilemedi', yet red-card counts exist for 69% of rows and 100% since 2018, and shots/SOT for 66%. Opponent red cards are the leading benign explanation for HT-behind-then-win. As written, matches with a red card would be listed as 'unexplained'. (d) Nothing forbids aggregating or ranking anomaly scores by team, league or referee. A per-team anomaly count works as an implicit label even when no single row carries one.
issues.fix: Define PREDICTIVE_PATTERN as a Mode B result with a pattern status, and UNEXPLAINED_ANOMALY as a single match whose surprise is above a pre-registered quantile (e.g. the top 0.5% of −log2 p within its league-season) and is not explained by the checks that can be run. Add the red-card check (and the SOT ratio when available) to the checklist with the result 'açıklanabilir: kırmızı kart'. Forbid team, league or referee aggregates and rankings of anomaly scores in both the UI and the reports, and add a test that enforces this. Keep the official-decision fields (source, date, scope, appeal/finality) and the rule against using a decision before its date.

issues.section: Missing UI section (three views, statuses, historical vs pre-match separation)
issues.problem: The contract has no UI rules, yet the user requires three views (timeline, similar sequences, pattern validation card), the six statuses, a strict split between the historical screen and the pre-match screen, and a separate anomaly view. The UI map also omits the anomaly view. These are leakage rules, not cosmetics. The pre-match screen must not show POST_EVENT data, neighbours whose labels became known after decision_time, or statuses that the frozen experiment records do not support.
issues.fix: Add a §13 'Arayüz kuralları'. Historical screen: timeline with PRE/EVENT/POST blocks and Mode A summaries labelled 'olay seçimli'. Pre-match screen: only data with timestamp < decision_time and only neighbours with label_known_at < decision_time; no POST_EVENT; status read from the latest experiments.jsonl record; EXPLORATORY and INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE patterns shown greyed out with no probability adjustment. Validation card: the Mode B fields plus the falsification results. Anomaly page: separate, with no link to decide(), the ledger or the pattern status. Add a UI test that the pre-match view renders no POST_EVENT field.

issues.problem: The disclosure says only aggregate HT/FT frequencies and the PSV list were seen. Before the contract, however, understand/probe_joint_htft2.py computed tilted vs untilted HT/FT cell calibration and multiclass log-loss on all 52,902 usable rows from 2019-07-01 on, which is the test period. S0 (§6) then adopted the tilted + q-calibrated derivation. So S0's HT/FT construction has been examined against test-period outcomes, and the 'kapalı' label overstates how untouched the test is.
issues.fix: Add this probe to the disclosure. State that the tilted derivation follows from the user's 'A/B/C ile aynı dağılım' requirement, not from that comparison, and freeze it. Label the test period 'S0 İY/MS kalibrasyonu test döneminde görülmüş'. Name the forward paper period as the only fully clean evidence, and say so on every OUT_OF_SAMPLE_SUPPORTED card.

issues.problem: The budget and the multiplicity family cover only the 840-hypothesis atom search. Several other analyses are run without being counted or corrected: S0/S1/S2 log-loss comparisons on every target, the hazard LRT and its out-of-sample comparison, the A/B/C check of features 1–8 on the three main markets, and any post-event analysis. PAPER_TRADING has no minimum sample, end date or demotion rule, so forward tracking can run until it 'works'.
issues.fix: Pre-register a complete experiment list with a family label for each item. Analyses outside the atom family get Holm correction within their own family, and every item is logged in experiments.jsonl even when the result is null. For forward tracking, fix the evaluation point (e.g. at least N=300 qualifying team-rows or 2 seasons, whichever comes first), the success criterion (the same log-loss bootstrap rule as the test), and demotion to NO_ADDED_VALUE on failure, with no extension.

issues.section: Missing mandatory test list / no main-model-change gate
issues.problem: The contract does not map the user's mandatory test list to concrete tests. 'No main model change' is stated only for aliases (§1). In fact goals/joint.py, markets.py, model.py and value.py are already modified (git diff: +283 lines, adding htft_probs and the parse_htft path in validate_quote). The only regression evidence that A/B/C predictions and intervals are unchanged is the session-scoped scratchpad file seq/baseline_freeze.json versus baseline_after_htft.json, which is not a repo test.
issues.fix: Add a section listing each mandatory test with its pytest name. It covers: draw-code normalisation (H/D/A, 0, D, X); home/away flip; X/X vs 0-0; HT missing → UNKNOWN; unplayed next matches not filled; same-day and mirror-row exclusion; label_known_at purge; a later official decision not leaking; a random-target null that finds no strong pattern; the reference process recomputing atoms; byte-for-byte reproduction from manifest and seed; ROI_UNAVAILABLE for HTFT; the anomaly kept isolated from decide() and the ledger; the UI pre-match view showing no POST_EVENT. Move the m10_predict, m10_interval and label_frame hashes into tests/fixtures as a golden regression test that fails CI on any change to the primary markets.

issues.problem: 'GERIDEN_GALIBIYET' reads in Turkish as 'comeback win', the in-match concept the contract itself declares DATA_QUALITY_BLOCKED, so UI users will misread the HT-behind-then-win target. §8 says coach and squad eras are 'veri yok' but does not give them the formal DATA_QUALITY_BLOCKED status. Its 'henüz gözlenmedi' hazard category also mixes left-truncation at the data start with newly promoted teams.
issues.fix: Rename the targets to IY_GERIDE_MS_GALIP, IY_ONDE_MS_MAGLUP and so on, and keep 'maç içi geri dönüş' as a separate DATA_QUALITY_BLOCKED target in the UI. Mark coach/squad eras and all-official-match counts DATA_QUALITY_BLOCKED in the interval view. Split 'henüz gözlenmedi' into 'veri başlangıcı (sol kesik)' and 'kapsama yeni giren'.

sound_parts: §2 HT/FT definitions: canonical 1/X/2 normalisation that includes the source's H/D/A codes; X/X kept distinct from 0-0; regulation time only; UNKNOWN when HT is missing; the home/away flip table for team targets; and the statement that HTFT_2_1 does not imply O3.5 or FH O1.5.
Both mirror rows share event_id/pair_id and move together in splits, the bootstrap and the reference process.
§3 unplayed next matches stay censored and are not filled with zeros or failures; the opponent's history follows the same rules.

§4 decision_time at match-day 00:00 with every same-day match excluded; label_known_at plus purge at period boundaries; S2 excludes the query match, its mirror row and same-day rows; later official decisions never enter earlier computations.
§7 reference process: one HT/FT draw per match, all history atoms recomputed, the whole 840-hypothesis search re-run on each replicate, WY max-|z| plus BY, and the limits stated honestly.
§5 period table: discovery, parameter, test and forward paper are separate, and the 2026/27 matches that predate the contract are excluded from the forward period.
§10 ROI_UNAVAILABLE for HTFT and comeback targets, with no HT/FT odds derived from 1X2, and the similarity score never added to a probability.
§12 manifest (data SHA, commit, seed, tz-aware timestamp, hypothesis count) and keeping every experiment, including negative and inconclusive ones.

lens: Data semantics and feasibility. I checked the contract against understand_maps.json, the walk_forward code (validation.py:24-44) and read-only probes of home30/matches.pkl. The probe scripts are in the scratchpad (rv_a.py to rv_f.py). Nothing in the repo was modified.

issues.problem: The null draws only one 9-cell HT/FT outcome per match, yet it is supposed to recompute 'all atoms that depend on past results' from the draws. The atom SON10_2Y_GOL_FARKI_EN_AZ_5 and S1 feature 7 (second-half goal difference over the last 10 matches) need goal counts. An HT/FT sign cannot supply them. There are two ways this can go wrong. (a) The atom keeps real goal differences while outcomes are simulated. The null is then not the process the contract describes, and conditions using this atom have a different support distribution in the replicates than in the real data. (b) The atom cannot be computed at all. Either way the single-step Westfall-Young max|z| reference is wrong for every hypothesis that involves this atom: 19 of the 210 conditions, i.e. 76 of the 840 hypotheses.
issues.fix: State that each replicate draws a full score path from S0. First draw the H1 score from S0's 11x11 H1 grid. Then draw H2 goals from S0's conditional Poisson rates with the state multipliers. Apply the M10 region tilt by rejection sampling with acceptance w_r/max(w), or by reweighting. From that single draw derive HT/FT, FT points and second-half goal difference. Cache the per-match H1 cell probabilities and H2 rates once: for about 62.8k discovery matches that is 62.8k x 121 floats, roughly 61 MB. Add an acceptance test: across replicates, the simulated 9-cell frequencies must match S0's 9 probabilities within Monte Carlo error.

issues.problem: S0 is recalibrated separately for each team target with a 2-parameter logistic. That makes mirror rows incoherent. The home GERIDEN_GALIBIYET row and the away ONDEN_MAGLUBIYET row are the same event (HTFT_2_1), yet they get two different probabilities. Two contract statements then conflict. E = Σp0 uses 'S0' without saying recalibrated or raw, while the null draws from S0's raw 9 HT/FT probabilities. The inspection measured S0 under-predicting the reversal cells 1/2 and 2/1 by about 7-12% relative, in-sample. Suppose E is raw. A large single-atom condition such as EV_SAHIBI x GERIDEN_GALIBIYET has about 62.8k discovery home rows and E around 1,600. A 10% excess then gives z around 4 in the real data and z around 0 in the null, so a pure calibration artefact passes FWER. It would also replicate in the parameter period, because the miscalibration persists. Suppose instead E is recalibrated. Then the null replicates are not centred on E, and the max|z| distribution is distorted.
issues.fix: Recalibrate once, at match level, on the 9 home-perspective cells: a multinomial logistic on log S0 cell probabilities, fitted on prior seasons only. Derive every team-target p0 from that recalibrated 9-vector through the section 2 mapping, so mirror rows are coherent by construction. Draw the null from the same recalibrated distribution that E uses. Add a pre-search calibration gate: in discovery, the global O/E for each of the 4 targets, split by home and away, must have a 95% interval containing 1. Otherwise stop and report S0 miscalibration instead of searching.

issues.problem: S0 is unavailable or degenerate where discovery starts. The contract says warm-up 2000/01-2003/04 trains S0, but walk_forward keeps only fold > BURN_IN_LAST=2002. Fold 2004/05 is therefore trained on 2003/04 alone. That season has 5,160 matches and is fragmentary: D2 has 15 matches, F2 15, SP2 158, F1 223 (59%), D1 and I1 194 (63%), I2 59%. The >=2000-row rule passes anyway. Three consequences follow. (a) League conditions for D2, F2 and SP2 in 2004/05 are fitted on almost nothing. (b) The recalibration needs earlier seasons' out-of-sample S0 predictions. There are none for 2004/05, because 2003/04 has no S0 prediction, and only one season exists for 2005/06. (c) FORM_BEKLENTI_USTU/ALTI and S1 feature 6 need S0 expected points for the team's previous 10 matches. Those fall in 2003/04, where no out-of-sample S0 exists, so these atoms are undefined for about the first 10 team matches of 2004/05. The contract gives no NA rule. On top of this, 2004/05 is itself partial in 9 leagues (I2 20%, E2 68%, E1 71%, SP1 71%, N1 74%).
issues.fix: Pick and record one S0 training definition: either walk_forward as-is, or an own loop that includes 2000-2002 rows only after a per-team burn-in. Make 2004/05-2005/06 S0 out-of-sample warm-up seasons. In those seasons, S0 predictions are produced only to fit the recalibration and to supply expected points, and no hypotheses are evaluated. Move the discovery start to 2006/07. If the 2004/05 start is kept, the contract must instead state identity recalibration for 2004/05, and set S0-dependent atoms to NA (rows dropped from the conditions that use them) whenever any of the 10 S0 expectations is missing. The same rule must apply in the null.

issues.section: 7 ('2003/04 ısınma satırlarında çekim lig-sezon taban frekanslarından')
issues.problem: The null's treatment of pre-discovery history is incomplete and internally inconsistent. Atom 8, OLAYDAN_BERI_20_USTU and OLAYDAN_BERI_EN_FAZLA_3 can look back up to 60 matches, which is 2 or more seasons, i.e. into 2001/02-2002/03. The contract says nothing about those seasons in the null. For 2003/04, base-rate draws ignore team strength, so the simulated history is decoupled from S0 strength and FAVORI. Early-discovery support counts and the correlation structure of history atoms with FAVORI and EV_SAHIBI then differ systematically between the real data and the null, which biases the max|z| reference. There is also no reason to simulate warm-up rows at all, since hypotheses are evaluated only on discovery rows.
issues.fix: Make the null conditional on the real past. In every replicate, rows dated before the first evaluated season keep their real outcomes, and only rows in the evaluated period are simulated. The base-rate rule is then not needed. If simulation of warm-up rows is kept, specify it for every row before the evaluated period, not just 2003/04, and draw from S0-like strength-aware probabilities.

issues.problem: The alias approach is neither complete nor safe as described. (a) A deterministic intra-season rule finds 3 splits in December 2024: MGladbach to M'gladbach (D1), Nottm Forest to Nott'm Forest (E0), and Preussen Munster to Preußen Münster (D2). The rule is: two names in the same league-season, non-overlapping date ranges, never meeting each other. The contract's example list omits Preußen Münster. (b) Fuzzy cross-season matching proposes many pairs that are different clubs: Granada 74/Granada (identical after normalisation), Murcia/UCAM Murcia, Gaziantepspor/Gaziantep, Malatyaspor/Yeni Malatyaspor, Airdrie/Airdrie Utd, Extremadura/Extremadura UD, Rouen/Quevilly Rouen, Aves/AVS, Wimbledon/AFC Wimbledon. It misses low-similarity true renames such as Sparta/Sparta Rotterdam (similarity 0.57). (c) 'Ana modeller etkilenmez' is false for this module. S0 is built from goals/features.py, which keys Elo and DC state on raw names. After the December 2024 renames, S0 treats Nott'm Forest, M'gladbach and Preußen Münster as new promoted teams in the test period (Elo at the 20% quantile, DC promoted priors). Their S0 errors line up with the FORM_BEKLENTI and SON5 atoms. Raw-name team counts are also inflated: E0 2024/25 has 21 names, D1 and D2 19, which breaks SEZON_SONU.
issues.fix: Use a two-tier map. Tier 1 merges automatically, but only intra-season splits found by the deterministic rule above, with a unit test. Tier 2 holds cross-season merges, accepted only from a manually reviewed list that cites a rename source. The default is 'different identity': the old spell is right-censored and the new one left-truncated. Document a policy for refounded or successor clubs (recommended: no merge). Apply the map before building S0's input features in the research pipeline, using a research-only feature build keyed by canonical id. If that is not done, flag the affected teams' rows and exclude them from the search and the test for their first 10 matches after the rename. Acceptance test: after mapping, each non-split league-season with full coverage has n canonical ids, and each id has 2(n-1) matches.

issues.problem: A day threshold cannot detect the data holes that actually occur. Within-season holes: in discovery, 2004/05 is incomplete in D2 (89%), E0 (88%), E1 (71%), E2 (68%), E3 (80%), I1 (79%), I2 (20%), N1 (74%) and SP1 (71%). In 2007/08, F2 is at 92%, N1 at 90% and P1 at 87%. In the test period, EC 2024/25 is at 33%. The missing matches are scattered month by month: E1 2004/05 has between 9 and 70 per month. B1 2009/10-2022/23 contains only the 28-30 regular-season matches, with the play-offs absent, while B1 2023/24 onward includes the post-split rounds. G1 likewise lacks pre-2019 play-offs, and G1 2024/25 stops at 24 matches. As a result, 'last 5/10', 'matches since the event', rest days and the season match index silently skip unrecorded matches. An event in a missing match is unobserved yet counted as a non-event. Separately, some one-season absences are shorter than 400 days and get bridged silently: Dresden (D2 2019/20 to 2021/22, 391 days) and Perugia (I2, 386 days), both because of the COVID calendar.
issues.fix: Base spell and window validity on a split-aware coverage matrix plus season continuity, not on days. A window or count is valid only if (i) every league-season it touches has at least 97% of its scheduled matches, using a per-league-season format table, and (ii) the team's season labels are consecutive, with no skipped season. Otherwise it is NA, both in the real data and in the null. Keep 400 days only as a secondary guard. Report the share of discovery rows lost. Either treat post-regular-season rounds uniformly (exclude them from targets and windows in all seasons) or flag them explicitly.

issues.problem: The rule 'match index ≥ 0.8 × 2 × (number of teams − 1)' assumes a double round robin. Measured on the data, it flags 52% of team rows in SC0 (12 teams, 38 matches, threshold 17.6), 58-59% in SC1-SC3 (10 teams, 36 matches, threshold 14.4), 23% in B1 and 26% in G1, against about 19-21% everywhere else. In the Scottish leagues the atom therefore means 'second half of the season', and its pairwise conditions mix league identity into the hypothesis. Three further problems: team counts taken from the data are distorted by aliases; index counts are wrong in partial seasons; and with section 5's date-based season, the 554 COVID-restart matches of July-August 2020 (source label 2019/20, in 9 leagues) would become the first matches of 2020/21.
issues.fix: Define stage as the team's match index in the source season label (not season_year) divided by L, where L is the scheduled regular-season length for that league-season from the static format table (SC0 33, SC1-SC3 36, B1 30 or 34, G1 26/30/34, others 2(n−1) with n taken from the format table). Post-split rounds either get their own stage value or are excluded. Stage is NA in league-seasons with less than 97% coverage.

issues.problem: The contract does not say whether team windows cross covered leagues. Twelve of the 22 leagues form tier chains: E0-EC, D1/D2, I1/I2, SP1/SP2, F1/F2 and SC0-SC3. The existing builders keep state per league. They do not reset forms (Norwich carried ppg6 from 2014/15), and they give every new team Elo at the 20% quantile plus DC promoted priors. This was verified with Newcastle, Aston Villa and Norwich, all at Elo 1410.8 in E1 2016/17. S0 therefore systematically underrates clubs relegated into a covered league early in the season. Those same rows tend to carry SON5_GALIBIYETSIZ, SON3_MAGLUBIYET and FORM_BEKLENTI_ALTI from last season's higher tier, which produces spurious 'bounce-back' patterns that are really S0 artefacts. The null cannot catch this, because it assumes S0 is true.
issues.fix: Build windows on canonical team id across all covered leagues and carry a 'league changed since the previous match' flag. Add a non-searched control for the first 8 matches after a league change (separately for promotion and relegation) to the S0 recalibration, or exclude those rows from the search. Require surviving candidates to hold on the subset with no league change. Report the S0p comparison for them.

issues.problem: With R = 200 replicates, the smallest permutation p-value is 1/201 ≈ 0.005. The Benjamini-Yekutieli threshold at rank 1 for m = 840 is 0.05/(840 × H(840)), with H(840) ≈ 7.31, which is about 8.1e-6. BY can therefore never reject anything if its per-hypothesis p-values come from the replicates. Getting per-hypothesis permutation p-values small enough would take about 120k replicates, which is not feasible. The selection rule 'düzeltilmiş p < 0,05' does not say which correction is the gate.
issues.fix: Name single-step Westfall-Young max|z| as the only selection gate (its p resolution of 1/201 is enough for 0.05). Compute BY only from analytic marginal p-values (Poisson mid-p, or normal from z) and label it descriptive. In each replicate, recompute the support filter (n ≥ 500, E ≥ 25) on the simulated atoms, and take the max only over hypotheses that pass it.

issues.problem: The contract defines UNKNOWN only for the target. The 102 HT-missing matches are clustered (T1 2022/23: 29, G1 2014/15: 22, SP2 2018/19: 21), so they fall inside many windows in those leagues. HT-dependent counts (atoms 1-4, SON5_IY_*, RAKIP_*ONDE*, OLAYDAN_BERI_*) have no stated rule. The null will also draw HT for these rows unless they are masked, which would give the replicates information the real data does not have.
issues.fix: State the rules. An HT-dependent window count is NA if any match in the window has unknown HT. FT-only atoms are unaffected. 'Matches since the event' becomes NA once the gap since the last event contains an HT-unknown match. In the null, re-mask these 102 rows to UNKNOWN after drawing.

issues.problem: The store drops HTResult and FTResult (parsers.py:34-37), so the store holds only scores. Code normalisation therefore matters only for future sources. There, mapping a bare '0' to X is risky: in numeric columns, 0 can be a parse default. The contract also does not define 'çelişkili'.
issues.fix: Derive HT/FT labels only from hthg/htag/fthg/ftag. Use source codes (H→1, D→X, A→2) only as a consistency check (0 mismatches verified on the mirror). Accept '0' as a draw code only where a source's codebook declares it. Define 'çelişkili' as HT goals greater than FT goals for either side, or a code/score mismatch.

issues.problem: In discovery, 13,885 of 125,646 team rows have league rest of 3 days or less. They are concentrated in the English E1-EC leagues (E1 26% of rows, EC 33%) against P1 at 0.2% and G1 at 0.9%. Teams with midweek cup or European matches are recorded with long rest. The atom therefore measures league fixture congestion, not rest. The contract also does not say what value rest takes at a team's first match or after a spell break.
issues.fix: Rename the atom to a league-congestion name. Set rest to NA, not 30, at the first observed match and after any spell break. Interpret any finding as within-league congestion only.

sound_parts: Section 2 team-perspective mapping table: I checked every row and each is correct. With 1 = home, GERIDEN_GALIBIYET is home 2_1 / away 1_2, ONDEN_MAGLUBIYET is home 1_2 / away 2_1, BERABERLIKTEN_GALIBIYET is X_1 / X_2, and ONDEN_BERABERLIK is 1_X / 2_X. The example (HT 0-1, FT 2-1: HTFT_2_1 yes, B and C no) is right. The counts are consistent: 8,386 = 4,711 + 3,675.
Section 1 data facts match the verified values: 184,378 matches, 184,276 with HT (102 missing), no team plays twice on one day, kickoff times only from 2019/20, and no HT/FT odds.
event_id/pair_id clustering, and keeping the two rows of a match in the same ISO week for bootstrap and null, are correct. No duplicates exist on (league, date, home, away).
Right-censoring at data end and label_known_at for 'next k matches' targets are specified correctly. Leaving 2026/27 matches dated before the contract out of forward tracking is correct.

Computational feasibility is fine. S0 needs about 22 per-season M10 refits: the final test ran 8 folds with 4 variants plus challengers in 588 s, so this is minutes. The HT/FT grid takes about 14.6 s per 52.9k rows, so about 50 s for all rows. The R=200 null runs on the discovery team rows only (about 125.6k, not 368k). With S0 probabilities cached and no feature rebuild, each replicate is O(N) rolling team counts plus 210 masks x 4 sums, which is seconds per replicate and minutes in total. The full-score sampling grid fits in memory (about 61 MB).
